decision: read the three GPU kernels as SPIR-V text and as LLVM IR, with tools from the repo's pinned nixpkgs
why: the kernels are the only statement of the pixel math
result: preprocess, ltm_gain and postprocess decoded by hand, ids noted

decision: will not run Samsung's SPIR-V kernels on the GPU, only read them
why: kickoff says never execute anything from the driver package
result: kernel arithmetic stays a reading, flagged as not provable

decision: decompiled the CPU side of the five tone-mapping calculators in intelic.dll by string cross-reference, in a private Ghidra project
why: the kernels take float arguments (grid scale, guide weight, a/b/c, matrices, filter strength) whose values are set on the CPU
evidence: scripts/pe_refs.py, scripts/icdec.sh, ic/gain.c ic/filter.c ic/post.c ic/preopen.c ic/resize.c
result: grid scale 15/(N-1), guide weight and bias /8192, b and c /255, yuv2rgb /m[0], rgb2yuv /(m0+m1+m2), filter new=0.3 old=0.7 first frame copied

decision: read the PAL kernel's init and compute functions and Samsung's nntm_control record
why: need to know which parameters are constants and which move per frame
result: matrices, a/b/c, guide weight/bias are tuning constants; the blend map is per frame: global_weight and radial_dependency_weight interpolated by sensor gain, shaped by the lens shading grid, cut inside a detected face

decision: wrote the literal half-precision Python reference and ran it on recorded frames
why: numpy float16 does each operation in float32 and rounds to half, which equals IEEE half arithmetic for add, sub, mul and div
result: runs in 2.7 s per 1080p frame; shadows 1st percentile 37 to 29, 99th 207 to 209, picture gains contrast

decision: blend map built from the F11 lens shading table of the aiqb
why: the five light sources give falloff maps within 0.005 of each other, so the choice does not matter; F11 is the indoor one
evidence: extract.py shading(); comparison printed in the run transcript
result: centre weight 1.0, corners 0.16

decision: chose exact half-precision emulation in the element over plain float32
why: the Windows kernels compute in half; rounding each float32 operation to half reproduces them and makes the comparison with the reference an equality, not a tolerance
result: built

decision: first run of the element against the reference on 6 consecutive frames of t1_1080_verbose, full range
why: the comparison is the test
result: 0 differing bytes of 3110400 in every frame; output differs from input by up to 14 codes so the work ran

decision: ran element against reference on 3 recordings x 2 ranges x 6 frames plus identity grid
why: pass condition: equal within 1 code on three recorded frames; identity returns input within 1
result: element equals reference exactly (0) in all 36 frames; identity differs from input by up to 9 codes on about 50 pixels per frame, all outside the RGB gamut where the Windows kernel clamps; in-gamut pixels differ by at most 1

decision: Nix derivation builds by path and runs check.py on a synthetic clip in installCheckPhase
why: the comparison with the reference is the test
result: builds in 21 s on the remote builder; first build showed element vs reference 1 because the reference let OpenVINO use all threads; with 1 inference thread on both sides the difference is 0

decision: baseline timing of the one-vector-at-a-time kernel, one or two runs, machine at load 3
why: need the limiter before changing anything
evidence: scripts/bench.sh t4/t1, perf stat on core 0: 77.6e9 cycles, 89.9e9 instructions for 300 frames
result: 4 threads 15.6 ms per frame (luma 2.3, network 0.8, apply 12.6); 1 thread 57.6 ms; 1.16 instructions per cycle, so the core waits on the 16-cycle multiply-round chain, not on throughput

decision: will advance several 8-pixel vectors together through each operation
why: independent chains side by side let the core overlap them; the rounding conversions then bound it at about 2 cycles per operation
evidence: kept the old kernel at bench/nntm.single-vector.c
result: open

decision: batched kernel at -O2 was no faster (63 ms single thread against 58)
why: perf stat showed 3 times the instructions at 3 times the instructions per cycle: the lane structs were copied through memory
evidence: scripts/quick.sh: O2 batched 2.04G cycles 6.22G instructions for 6 frames
result: kept the batched kernel, changed the optimisation level

decision: build with -O3, batch of 64 pixels
why: '-O3 unrolls the lane loops and removes the copies; batch 64 beat 32 and 16
evidence: scripts/quick.sh: O3 0.87G cycles; step 32 0.92G; step 16 1.14G; all outputs equal the reference
result: single thread 22 ms per frame (was 58), 4 threads 7.3 ms (was 15.6), one run each at machine load 9

decision: ruled out denormal assists as the cause of the slow first kernel
why: half-subnormal values are common here and conversions of them could have trapped to microcode
result: not the cause

decision: five-run benchmark of the Nix build on a quiet machine (load 1.4 to 3.5)
why: throughput pass condition
evidence: scripts/bench.sh, bench/lim4.* full4.* lim1.* lim2.* lim8.* bypass.*; earlier set at load 9 in bench/loaded9/
result: 4 threads limited 7.95 ms per frame (range 7.92 to 8.18), full 7.42; 1 thread 23.8; 2 threads 12.9; 8 threads 5.4; at load 9 the 4-thread median was 8.63

decision: measured what the half rounding costs with a build that skips it
why: name the limiter from a run, not from reading code
result: single thread 23.7 ms exact against 13.1 ms without rounding: 45 percent of the time is the two conversions per operation; the rest is the arithmetic itself

decision: multi-second frames under 16 busy loops traced to the harness, not the element
why: ananicy-cpp puts nix into SCHED_IDLE and gst-launch inherited it when started through nix develop
evidence: /etc/ananicy.d nix rule BG_CPUIO sched idle; bench.sh now starts gst-launch directly and records class and nice in each .wall file
result: with class TS the worst frame under 16 hogs is 0.4 s once, typically 35 to 60 ms

decision: tried ending a row pass when its chunks are done instead of when every helper checks in, then reverted it
why: written while chasing the stall above; A/B under 16 hogs showed no difference beyond run-to-run spread
evidence: bench/sat_old_paced.* 24.0 ms (21.3 to 26.3) vs sat_new_paced.* 23.7 (21.5 to 33.0); flat 30.7 vs 29.3 with overlapping ranges
result: reverted to the stack-allocated sweep that the verified build uses

decision: final quiet-machine benchmark with the corrected harness, 5 alternating runs of 300 frames per setting
why: throughput pass condition
evidence: bench/lim4.* full4.* lim1.* lim2.* lim8.* bypass.*, scripts/bench_report.py, scripts/late.py
result: 4 threads: limited 7.90 ms per frame (range 7.80 to 7.95) = 127 fps, full 7.33 ms = 136 fps, no frame over 12.1 ms in 1500; 1 thread 23.85 ms; 2 threads 12.88; 8 threads 5.41

decision: load tests paced at 30 fps, 5 runs each, pipeline in class TS at the same nice as the busy loops
why: the pass condition asks for 30 fps with other load
result: 8 of 16 cores busy: median 13.7 ms, 1.7 percent of frames over 33.3 ms; all 16 busy: median 23.9 ms, 13.3 percent late (4.2 percent with 8 threads, 3.9 percent with the load 10 nice levels lower); every run of 300 frames still finished in 10.2 s

decision: before/after frames, 100 percent crops, gain maps and metrics for three recordings, 60 consecutive frames each
why: pass condition asks for images and plain statements on shadows, local contrast, halo and flicker
result: 1st percentile luma 37-39 to 31-32, 99th up 3-4, local contrast x1.08-1.11, fine detail and noise x1.10-1.14, frame-to-frame block change x1.09-1.11, change next to a strong edge about 4 codes larger than 64 px away

decision: removed __pycache__, added a section on the element to DERIVATION.md, final Nix build
why: src = ./. copies the whole directory, so leftovers change the store path
result: check phase passed (element vs reference 0 in both ranges); plugin differs from the benchmarked build in 58 of 77856 bytes, the embedded store path

decision: reran the comparison matrix on the final artifact
why: the final store path is the one that ships
result: element equals reference exactly on 36 frames (3 recordings x 2 ranges x 6 frames); identity grid moves 124 to 506 pixels of 12.4 million by more than 1 code, all in blocks with an out-of-gamut pixel, in-gamut worst 1

decision: correction to the baseline row (one-vector kernel, 15.6 ms at 4 threads): its logs no longer exist
why: they were deleted when the first five-run set started; the numbers survive only in the session transcript
evidence: bench/nntm.single-vector.c is the kernel that was timed
result: baseline is a one-or-two-run ballpark, not reproducible from saved logs

decision: correction to the first quiet-machine row (7.95 ms): its files moved
why: the set was taken through nix develop before the harness fix, so it was archived when the corrected set replaced it
evidence: bench/quiet-via-nix/, and the earlier set at load 9 in bench/loaded9/
result: superseded by the corrected-harness row (7.90 ms)

decision: the first load test (16 busy loops, 170 s) was discarded
why: the busy loops expired after the first paced and the first flat-out run, so runs 2 to 5 measured an idle machine
evidence: bench/hog16_paced.*, bench/hog16_flat.*; later tests print the count of busy loops still alive at the end
result: replaced by the sat_* and half_* sets

decision: worker threads come from a GLib thread pool that claims 16-row chunks, not from OpenMP
why: libgomp threads spin after each parallel region and the wait policy can only be set by an environment variable; the pool sleeps between frames
result: not measured against OpenMP

decision: caps accept only widths that are multiples of 64 instead of handling a row tail
why: the kernel advances 64 pixels at a time and every mode of this camera (1920, 1280, 960, 640) fits; other widths fail negotiation instead of needing scratch copies
result: gst-inspect shows width [64, 2048, 64]

decision: kept the default of 4 threads
why: with 8 of 16 cores busy 4 and 8 threads were alike (1.1 to 1.7 against 1.3 percent late frames); with all 16 busy 8 threads cut late frames from 13.3 to 4.2 percent; on a quiet machine 4 threads already leave 4 times headroom
result: threads stays a property; 8 is the setting for a machine that is always saturated

decision: no cross-model review of this trail was run
why: the kickoff forbids starting agents
result: flagged in the report
